page.layout: One printed page, numbered 185. Running head at top ("Sect.14. CONTRA MERITA, &c."). Below it, one centred column: heading "II. Thesis.", the italic thesis statement, the section heading "SECT. XIIII.", then the running text in one column. No notes in the margins. Left-edge fragments belong to the neighbouring page and right-edge marks are show-through, so both are excluded. Signature "A a" at the foot.

main_text.l: II. Thesis.
SECT. XIIII.
EXtant hodie in Collecta, in Commemoratione
pro defunctis, haec verba; Memento

l.i: Domine, &c. Et famulis tuis, de multitudine miserationum
& societatem digneris cum tuis sanctis: in quor-
um consortium nos, non Æstimator meriti, sed
venia Largitor, admittas, per Christum Dominum

main_text.l: nostrum. Haec sunt Collectae verba, quae
plane contradicunt dogmati superiori ejus-
dem Ecclesiae, Ex meritis Christi habemus

l.i: nos virtutem merendi, juxta aequalitatem justitiae,
quae exigat praemium vitae aeternae apud

main_text.l: Deum. Haec duo si inter se conferantur, quis
satis mirari potest horum hominum stupo-
rem, qui in orando Deum non esse Æstima-
torem meritorum suorum docent, in definiendo
tamen & concludendo Æstimatorem meritorum
suorum esse decernunt? Rursus, doctrinā
hac, Merendi virtutem suam per Merita
Christi jactant; oratione tamen, per Christum
(adeoque per ejus Merita) veniam deprecan-
tur, nè ex Meritis suis dijudicentur. Dicent
fortasse, Professionem eorum de Meritis esse
de Fide; Orationem autem Spei duntaxat esse
sobolem.

page.notes: Printed text is clear throughout. Possible doubtful readings: "nè" (printed with a grave accent) and "doctrinā" (the final vowel mark is faint). Long s is normalised to s. No Greek or Hebrew on the page. Left-edge fragments (from the neighbouring page) and right-edge show-through were excluded.
